purpose: The verified prior art for issue #111's subspace / product-manifold research family. Every entry names the provider query that returned it, its access level, the exact mathematical overlap with the target family, and what it forbids a future proposal from claiming. No entry is a claim of novelty: this is the prior-art side of the review.

store.note: The single paper identity store is #110's (tools/harness2_genrec/literature.py + results/hyperbolic_research_runs/literature/). This matrix is a curated view over it and adds no second identity store. Papers are deduplicated by identifier; the raw accumulated store holds 109 records across 10 queries.

entries.title: Structure-Aligned History Learning with Subspace-Structured Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
entries.query: Structure-Aligned History Learning with Subspace-Structured Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation
entries.access_note: the abstract was retrieved through OpenAlex (verified_abstract_only) and the official reference implementation was read directly (genrec/models/SAHL/codebook_generators.py, README.md). No equation was taken from the paper PDF; the mathematics below is quoted from the released code, which is the stronger evidence.

what_it_already_does: SRBQ (SubspaceResidualBalancedGenerator): one global PCA with whiten=True over the item text embeddings, the resulting principal components split into G contiguous groups of equal width (srbq_n_groups default 4), and within each group digits_per_group = K/G digits produced by residual quantisation (each digit K-means over the running residual, then residual = residual - centers[labels]).

An occupancy cap on the assignment: target_size = n_items / codebook_size, max_size = target_size * balance_ratio (default 2.0), overflow members reassigned to the nearest cluster with spare capacity, centres re-estimated, iterated srbq_balance_iters (default 3) times, and a hard failure if any cluster still exceeds max_size.
Ablations shipped in the same class: no_subspace (n_groups = 1), no_residual, no_balance — i.e. the paper itself isolates exactly the three components the subspace family would claim.

MHL (Masked History Learning): multi-granularity masked-history reconstruction over token / subspace / item units (Tri-Mixed probabilities 0.33/0.33/0.34), an entropy-guided masking curriculum decaying to zero, and next-item prediction in the final phase.

SID length K is a free parameter: 16 (Beauty), 32 (Toys, Sports), 64 (CDs) in the released configurations, with a codebook vocabulary of 256 per digit, a 2-layer 4-head GPT-2 backbone (hidden 448), and item text embeddings from Sentence-T5-base.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: Euclidean throughout: PCA (scikit-learn, whiten=True), K-means, scipy cdist with metric='euclidean'. There is no hyperbolic, spherical or product-manifold component in the quantiser.
what_it_does_not_do: It does not assign roles to the subspaces: the G groups are contiguous PCA blocks of decreasing variance, not a semantic factor, a behaviour factor or a uniqueness factor. Nothing in the code conditions a group on history or on the transition graph.
It does not use the item-item transition graph or any behaviour pair: the quantiser reads sentence embeddings only, and the history enters only through MHL's reconstruction objective.
It does not fit the frozen 3-token / 3x256 / 32-dim protocol: K = 16..64 digits, and the backbone, embedding source and evaluation protocol are all different.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids, in this repository, any claim that 'split the representation into subspaces, group the SID by subspace, cap each code's occupancy, and align the quantiser with history reconstruction' is new. A #111 proposal that is PCA-block + balanced residual quantisation + a history auxiliary is SAHL in a different notation. What remains open is the part SAHL does not do: a NON-Euclidean factor geometry with an explicit role per factor, a routing rule that reads behaviour, and fitting that into 3 tokens rather than 16-64.

entries.title: Learning Mixed-Curvature Representations in Product Spaces
entries.query: Learning Mixed-Curvature Representations in Product Spaces
entries.access_note: the identity resolves: OpenAlex returns the record W2923452197 with this title, these four authors and venue 'International Conference on Learning Representations'. The publication year OpenAlex reports is 2018 (the arXiv posting); the conference year is 2019. OpenAlex returned no abstract for this record and arXiv's API was blocked, so no equation is quoted from it here.

what_it_already_does: Represents an object as a point in a product of component spaces of different constant curvature (Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic), with per-component dimensions and per-component curvature.
Learns the product representation end-to-end with the component metrics held fixed, i.e. the product manifold is a representation space, not an auxiliary loss.
Establishes the product of geometric factors as existing theory and as a working embedding construction.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: product of constant-curvature factors; the total space has non-constant sectional curvature.
what_it_does_not_do: It is not a quantiser: there is no codebook, no discrete token, no SID.
It has no role assignment and no behaviour or history supervision; the factors are jointly learned by the downstream task.
It has no 3-token output or generative-recommendation pipeline.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids claiming the product-manifold concept itself, or 'a product of hyperbolic factors with per-factor dimensions and curvature', as a contribution. #111 explicitly says this is a foundation, not novelty. A proposal may use it only as the substrate for a NEW mechanism (routing, quantisation, or coupling) that is itself testably new.

entries.title: Improving Heterogeneous Graph Learning with Weighted Mixed-Curvature Product Manifold
entries.query: product manifold representation learning mixed curvature factors

what_it_already_does: Argues that each component space of a product manifold contributes differently to expressing structure, and therefore should be WEIGHTED accordingly — the per-factor importance weighting is explicit.
Embeds heterogeneous graphs (multiple relation types) in a product of Euclidean / hyperbolic / spherical components.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: product of constant-curvature components with learned per-component weights.
what_it_does_not_do: No discrete quantisation and no SID.
The weighting is a per-component scalar, learned by the graph objective; there is no routing rule keyed on a behaviour signal and no role declaration.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids claiming 'per-factor weighting of a product manifold', or 'components contribute differently so weight them', as the new mechanism. It also sets the bar for Family B: a routing mechanism must be more than a learned scalar weight per factor.

entries.title: Switch Spaces: Learning Product Spaces with Sparse Gating
entries.query: product manifold representation learning mixed curvature factors

what_it_already_does: Sparse gating mechanisms that learn to choose, combine and switch product-space components depending on the input data, with specialisation.
This is data-dependent factor routing in a product of Euclidean and non-Euclidean (hyperbolic, spherical) manifolds.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: product of constant-curvature factors, input-dependent sparse gates.
what_it_does_not_do: No quantisation, no codebook, no SID, no generative recommendation.
The gate is learned from the raw input, not from a declared history/transition signal, and there is no claim about which factor holds which role.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids claiming 'route an item to one factor or another with a learned gate over a product of hyperbolic spaces' as new. Family B must differ mathematically: the routing must be driven by a declared history/behaviour statistic, must act through the actual quantiser, and must be distinguishable from a sparse learned gate.

entries.title: HVQ-VAE: Variational auto-encoder with hyperbolic vector quantization
entries.query: hyperbolic vector quantization semantic ID generative recommendation
entries.access_note: identity verified by Crossref (DOI, title, five authors, venue, 2025); no abstract text was returned, so no equation is quoted.

what_it_already_does: A vector-quantised auto-encoder whose codebook lives in hyperbolic space: intrinsic hyperbolic vector quantisation for image representation.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: hyperbolic codebook (the paper's title states vector quantisation in hyperbolic space).
what_it_does_not_do: Not sequential recommendation, no SID, no 3-token generative output.
Not a product/subspace decomposition: one manifold, one codebook.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids claiming 'put the codebook in hyperbolic space' (path B, intrinsic hyperbolic VQ) as the new mechanism. Any path-B proposal must add something beyond a hyperbolic codebook plus the usual commitment/quantisation losses.

entries.title: CoST: Contrastive Quantization based Semantic Tokenization for Generative Recommendation
entries.query: hyperbolic vector quantization semantic ID generative recommendation

what_it_already_does: Contrastive learning over the quantisation codebook so that the learned semantic tokens carry collaborative signal, in a generative-recommendation pipeline.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: Euclidean codebook with a contrastive objective.
what_it_does_not_do: No non-Euclidean geometry, no factor decomposition, no role assignment.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids claiming 'add a contrastive (or NCE) term to the codebook so the SIDs carry behaviour signal' as new. This matters because the repository's r8_01 arm is a directed L1 transition NCE, so both the paper and the repo already own that idea.

entries.title: Addressing Cross-Stage Decoupling of Semantic and Collaborative Signals in Generative Recommendation
entries.query: hyperbolic vector quantization semantic ID generative recommendation

what_it_already_does: Diagnoses exactly the transfer problem issue #111 starts from: a two-stage pipeline in which item tokenization is dominated by textual semantics with limited collaborative signal, so code assignments are misaligned with downstream generation, while the generation stage re-embeds codes from interaction data and loses the semantic content. It names this 'cross-stage information decoupling' and proposes to address it.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: not stated as non-Euclidean in the retrieved abstract.
what_it_does_not_do: The retrieved abstract does not claim a product or subspace geometry; its proposal is about aligning the two stages' information, not about factorising the representation.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids presenting 'the Stage2 SID and the Stage3 model disagree about what the SID means' as a new diagnosis. #111's motivation must therefore be stated as a mechanism question, not as a new observation, and a proposal must cite this paper as the existing diagnosis.

entries.title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 20th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys 2026)
entries.query: product manifold representation learning mixed curvature factors

what_it_already_does: Treats the prefix tree of a semantic ID as non-uniform and constructs the ID adaptively per branch — i.e. the branching structure of the SID is already an explicit, optimised object.
mathematical_overlap.geometry: not stated as non-Euclidean in the retrieved metadata.
what_it_does_not_do: No factor manifold; the object optimised is the tree, not a geometric decomposition.

entries.novelty_impact: Forbids claiming 'make the L1->L2 branching adaptive' as the mechanism. It also matters for #111's diagnostics: the L1->L2 branch count is already a first-class quantity in the literature, so a proposal must say what it changes about the branch *geometry*, not merely about the count.

entries.title: Product Manifold Flow Matching for Mixed-Type Tabular Data Generation
entries.query: product manifold representation learning mixed curvature factors

what_it_already_does: Generates data on a product manifold with flow matching: continuous transport on a product of factor geometries.

entries.title: Hyperbolic Residual Quantization: Discrete Representations for Data with Latent Hierarchies
entries.query: the targeted prior-art search for the next family

mathematical_overlap.what_it_already_does: Hierarchical data arise in countless domains, from biological taxonomies and organizational charts to legal codes and knowledge graphs. Residual Quantization (RQ) is widely used to generate discrete, multitoken representations for such data by iteratively quantizing residuals in a multilevel codebook. However, its reliance on Euclidean geometry can introduce fundamental mismatches that hinder modeling of hierarchical branching, necessary for faithful representation of hierarchical data. In this work, we propose Hyperbolic Residual Quantization (HRQ), which embeds data natively in a hyperbolic manifold and performs residual quantization using hyperbolic operations and distance metrics. By adapting the embedding network, residual computation, and distance metric to hyperbolic geometry, HRQ imparts an inductive bias that aligns naturally with hierarchical branching. entries.title: HypRQ-VAE: Hyperbolic Item Indexing for Long-Tail-Aware Generative Recommender Systems
entries.query: the targeted prior-art search for the next family

mathematical_overlap.what_it_already_does: Sequential recommender systems model user behavior as item ID sequences, while recent generative methods cast recommendation as a language modeling task using large language models (LLMs). While this paradigm incorporates rich textual semantics, it introduces a fundamental mismatch: LLMs operate on text tokens, whereas recommender systems depend on discrete item indices. This misalignment often leads to hallucinations in generative recommendations. Existing methods attempt to bridge this gap by learning item vocabularies in Euclidean space, but they struggle to model the inherent long-tail distribution of real-world catalogs, where a small number of head items dominate, and a vast number of tail items reflect users' niche preferences. entries.title: Mixed-curvature Variational Autoencoders
entries.query: the targeted prior-art search for the level-wise family

mathematical_overlap.what_it_already_does: Euclidean geometry has historically been the typical "workhorse" for machine learning applications due to its power and simplicity. However, it has recently been shown that geometric spaces with constant non-zero curvature improve representations and performance on a variety of data types and downstream tasks. Consequently, generative models like Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) have been successfully generalized to elliptical and hyperbolic latent spaces. While these approaches work well on data with particular kinds of biases e.g. tree-like data for a hyperbolic VAE, there exists no generic approach unifying and leveraging all three models. We develop a Mixed-curvature Variational Autoencoder, an efficient way to train a VAE whose latent space is a product of constant curvature Riemannian manifolds, where the per-component curvature is fixed or learnable. entries.title: Decoupled Residual Quantization for Robust Semantic IDs in Recommendation
entries.query: the targeted prior-art search for the level-wise family

mathematical_overlap.what_it_already_does: Semantic IDs represent items as shared discrete token sequences and have become a practical tool for recommendation and retrieval. Yet it remains difficult to tell why a tokenizer fails: poor quality may come from codebook underutilization, unstable decision boundaries, or geometric distortion of the embedding space. This paper develops a quantitative framework for diagnosing these failures through expected codeword overlap and effective codebook capacity. The former measures expected codeword confusion under retrieval-time perturbation, while the latter converts that confusion into an effective number of usable, well-separated codes. The framework links semantic boundary confusion to both code usage imbalance and Euclidean geometric constraints. entries.title: HyperVQ: MLR-based Vector Quantization in Hyperbolic Space
entries.query: the targeted prior-art search for the approved candidate's operator

mathematical_overlap.what_it_already_does: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. entries.title: Differentiable Optimized Product Quantization and Beyond
entries.query: the targeted prior-art search for the approved candidate's operator

mathematical_overlap.what_it_already_does: Vector quantization techniques, such as Product Quantization (PQ), play a vital role in approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNs) and maximum inner product search (MIPS) owing to their remarkable search and storage efficiency. However, the indexes in vector quantization cannot be trained together with the inference models since data indexing is not differentiable. To this end, differentiable vector quantization approaches, such as DiffPQ and DeepPQ, have been recently proposed, but existing methods have two drawbacks. First, they do not impose any constraints on codebooks, such that the resultant codebooks lack diversity, leading to limited retrieval performance. Second, since data indexing resorts to operator, differentiability is usually achieved by either relaxation or Straight-Through Estimation (STE), which leads to biased gradient and slow convergence.
